messages:
Ravi: handing off evening shift — quick FYI on a few soft degradations we saw today.
- KV prefetch error-rate: intermittent spikes ~16:10–16:35 UTC. Symptoms: prefix cache misses and slow cold-starts, ~0.4% 5m error-rate (baseline <0.05%). Alert kv-prefetch-error-rate is flapping.
- Encoder pool (eu-prod-encoders): 2 pods saw CPU saturation during a model rollout at 16:22; p95 latency bumped ~120ms.
- Telemetry noise: request-rate anomaly detector in eu-west is noisy (false positives), probably need threshold tune.
If you see kv-prefetch firing, don't page for single short flaps — only escalate if >1% sustained for 5m or if cache hit-rate drops <85%.
Marta: ack, I'm taking evening coverage. I'll keep kv-prefetch on the watchlist and handle encoder pool if it recurs. Is there a preferred drain flow for enc pods?
Kevin: short command if you need a manual eviction:
```
kubectl cordon enc-3 && kubectl drain enc-3 --ignore-daemonsets --force
```
Then check rollout: `kubectl rollout status ds/encoder-set -n prod`
Marta: thanks — prefer to use our helper if available, avoids changing autoscaler state.
Ravi: yup, use the helper instead: `scripts/oncall/drain-encoder enc-3` — it coordinates with the autoscaler and mutes alerting for 5m. Also left a canary with debug logging on enc-3 (tag: enc-3-canary).
alert-bot: [automated] 2 alerts suppressed for kv-prefetch-error-rate in the last 30m (suppression window auto-apply).
Marta: got the helper. I'll run the drain if it flaps again and watch logs on enc-3-canary. If latency doesn't settle after a drain+roll, I'll escalate to perf and ping @Kevin.
Ravi: leaving a short note in the rotation doc: https://docs.redwood/handovers/1765432100 — includes links to runbooks and the monitoring query.
Kevin: quick monitoring query for reference: `sum(rate(kv_prefetch_errors[5m])) / sum(rate(kv_prefetch_requests[5m])) * 100` — use that for % error-rate.
Marta: copied. I'll mute the anomaly detector if it keeps firing falsely; will update this thread with any action. :thumbsup:
